title: Practice Exam 2
description: Weighted toward streaming, pipelines, and table maintenance.

questions.prompt: A Structured Streaming job is configured with the trigger below. What is its behavior?

options.text: It processes all currently available data, in as many micro-batches as needed, then stops
It runs continuously, processing new data as it arrives
It processes exactly one micro-batch and then stops
It fails unless a processing-time interval is also supplied

questions.explanation: `availableNow=True` drains everything available at start-up across multiple batches, then terminates — which keeps memory bounded on large backlogs. The older `once=True` processed a single batch; omitting the trigger entirely gives a continuously running micro-batch stream.

questions.prompt: In the Delta Live Tables definition below, what happens to an incoming record whose `amount` is null?

options.text: The record is discarded and counted as a violation in the pipeline event log
The pipeline update fails immediately
The record is written through with a null amount and flagged
The record is routed automatically to a quarantine table

questions.explanation: `ON VIOLATION DROP ROW` drops failing records while still reporting them in the event log metrics. `FAIL UPDATE` is the variant that halts the pipeline; with no `ON VIOLATION` clause the record is retained and only reported.

questions.prompt: A Delta table written by a frequent streaming job has accumulated thousands of small files, and queries have slowed. Which command addresses this directly?

options.text: OPTIMIZE
VACUUM
ANALYZE TABLE
REFRESH TABLE

questions.explanation: `OPTIMIZE` compacts many small files into fewer larger ones. `VACUUM` is unrelated — it deletes files no longer referenced by the transaction log to reclaim storage, and does not improve file layout.

questions.domain: ELT with Spark SQL and Python
questions.prompt: What distinguishes a shallow clone from a deep clone of a Delta table?

options.text: A shallow clone copies only metadata and continues to reference the source table's data files
A shallow clone copies the data but not the transaction history
A shallow clone can only be created within the source table's schema
A shallow clone is read-only and cannot be written to

questions.explanation: A shallow clone copies just the metadata, so it is near-instant but breaks if the source's files are vacuumed away. A deep clone copies the data files as well, producing a fully independent table. Both are writable.

questions.domain: ELT with Spark SQL and Python
questions.prompt: Which statement about a view created with `CREATE TEMP VIEW` is accurate?

options.text: It is scoped to the current SparkSession and disappears when that session ends
It is registered in the metastore and visible to all users
It materializes its query results to the table's storage location
It is visible to every notebook attached to the same cluster

questions.explanation: A temporary view is session-scoped and holds no data — the query re-runs on each reference. A *global* temporary view lives in the `global_temp` schema and is shared across sessions on the same cluster, which is the distinction option D describes.

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the group `analysts` read access to a Unity Catalog table?

options.text: GRANT SELECT ON TABLE sales.orders TO `analysts`
GRANT READ ON TABLE sales.orders TO `analysts`
ALLOW SELECT ON sales.orders FOR `analysts`
GRANT USAGE ON TABLE sales.orders TO `analysts`

questions.explanation: Reading a table requires the `SELECT` privilege. The group also needs `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA` on the containing objects — those traversal privileges are what `USAGE` covers in option D, and they are not sufficient on their own.
